requirements: Revalidate boot ID, UID, start ticks, executable, command hash, cgroup and service parent/main PID immediately before approval execution. Stop on any mismatch; do not chase replacement PIDs.
Open pidfds for the four validated Node processes; signal through those handles so PID reuse cannot target a replacement. Do not stop the systemd manager or flock parent.
Require each target initially running or sleeping, not already stopped. Record the exact intended set before any signal.

Start an independent watchdog with inherited pidfds outside the benchmark scope. Require an armed acknowledgement before the first STOP; watchdog restores the originally eligible set on 330-second expiry or supervisor-pipe EOF.

Supervisor restoration runs in finally and SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers. Stop benchmark children before releasing the quiet window. Watchdog remains armed until all intended processes are verified restored or exited.
After STOP, verify all four targets and their threads are stopped, CPU ticks cease and the measured CPUs are quiet before launching. Any failed check aborts and restores; no retry loop.
Run only the fixed sequential arms under the 300-second outer cap and 120-second per-arm caps. Retain partial outputs and failures.

On completion, CONT original pidfds only. Revalidate identities, resumed states/CPU activity, service state and peer/status logs; report connection or request failures. Do not auto-restart services or edit their policy.
Do not launch conditional quality comparison while workers remain paused for an unbounded repair session. Restore first; any later approved quiet window must have its own supervisor/watchdog receipt.

interruption_impact.meaning: STOP halts event loops and heartbeats but keeps process memory, GPU allocations and locks. In-flight requests may time out and peers may disconnect; CONT restores scheduling, not request success.
